milestones.description: Consider the sequence of nonzero reals x_1,x_2,x_3,... with x_n = x_{n-2}x_{n-1}/(2x_{n-2}-x_{n-1}) for n>2. Define y_k = 1/x_k. Formalize the problem: write the recurrence in terms of y, and state the target set S of pairs (x_1,x_2)∈(ℝ\{0})² for which |{n∈ℕ:x_n∈ℤ}| is infinite.

milestones.description: Using x_n = x_{n-2}x_{n-1}/(2x_{n-2}-x_{n-1}) and x_k≠0, compute 1/x_n exactly in terms of 1/x_{n-1} and 1/x_{n-2}. Write the linear recurrence satisfied by y_n = 1/x_n.

milestones.description: Assume x_1≠x_2. Set a=x_1-x_2, b=2x_2-x_1, K=x_1x_2 (all nonzero), and recall x_n=K/(a n+b). Show |a n+b|→∞ as |n|→∞, so |x_n|→0. Conclude |x_n|<1 for |n| large, hence only finitely many terms can be nonzero integers.

milestones.description: With the same a,b,K and x_n=K/(a n+b) for x_1≠x_2, solve |a||n|-|b|>|K| for |n|. Give an explicit bound N (in terms of |a|,|b|,|K|) such that |n|>N implies |x_n|<1.

milestones.description: Let a_1,...,a_5 be real. Define E = a_1a_2 + a_2a_3 + a_3a_4 + a_4a_5 + a_5a_1 and F = a_1a_3 + a_2a_4 + a_3a_5 + a_4a_1 + a_5a_2. Given E=20 and F=22. Define S = a_1^2 + a_2^2 + a_3^2 + a_4^2 + a_5^2. Goal: minimize S and write it as m + \sqrt{n}.

milestones.description: Define R_1 = \sum_{k=1}^{5} (a_k - a_{k+1})^2 with a_6 = a_1. Expanding gives R_1 = 2\sum a_k^2 - 2\sum_{adjacent} a_k a_{k+1} = 2S - 2E = 2S - 40. Thus S = 20 + R_1/2.

milestones.description: Define R_2 = \sum_{k=1}^{5} (a_k - a_{k+2})^2 with indices mod 5. Expanding gives R_2 = 2S - 2F = 2S - 44. Comparing with R_1 yields R_1 - R_2 = 4 identically.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF both formulas correct.

milestones.description: Set ω = e^{2πi/5}. For real a_k define c_j = \sum_{k=1}^{5} a_k ω^{-j k}, so c_0 = T ∈ ℝ and |c_4|=|c_1|, |c_3|=|c_2|. Parseval: \sum_{j=0}^{4}|c_j|² = 5S. For Q(d) = \sum_{k=1}^{5} a_k a_{k+d} (mod 5) we have Q(d) = (1/5)[c_0² + 2|c_1|² cos(2πd/5) + 2|c_2|² cos(4πd/5)]. Set A=|c_1|², B=|c_2|², X=c_0². Using Q(1)=20, Q(2)=22, cos72°=(\sqrt{5}-1)/4, cos144°=-(\sqrt{5}+1)/4, obtain: X + ((\sqrt{5}-1)/2)A - ((\sqrt{5}+1)/2)B = 100 and X - ((\sqrt{5}+1)/2)A + ((\sqrt{5}-1)/2)B = 110.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF system correctly expresses both equations with correct cosine coefficients.

milestones.description: Solve the system in X,A,B ≥ 0: X + ((\sqrt{5}-1)/2)A - ((\sqrt{5}+1)/2)B = 100 and X - ((\sqrt{5}+1)/2)A + ((\sqrt{5}-1)/2)B = 110. Subtracting gives (\sqrt{5}/2)(A-B) = -5 => B - A = 2\sqrt{5}. Adding gives X = 105 + (A+B)/2. Now S = (X+2A+2B)/5 = 21 + (A+B)/2 = 21 + A + \sqrt{5}. Since A ≥ 0, minimize at A=0 => B=2\sqrt{5}, X=105+\sqrt{5}, so S_min = 21+\sqrt{5}.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF S_min correct and achieved at A=0,B=2\sqrt{5}.

milestones.description: Define the game state after some moves have been made: let r be the remaining matches and let m be the number taken by the opponent on the previous move, so the current player may choose any integer x with 1 \le x \le \min(m,r). The player who makes r=0 wins. For the first move there is no previous move, so the first player chooses x with 1 \le x \le n-1 and leaves the state (n-x,x). The problem asks for all n>1 for which this initial choice can be forced into a losing state for the opponent.

milestones.note: ACCEPT IF state variables r,m,x and win condition are defined
hints: Define P-positions (previous player wins) and N-positions

milestones.description: If r \le m then the current player takes all r matches and wins immediately, so such states are N-positions. Hence every interesting state satisfies r>m \ge 1. Define a position to be P if every legal move leads to an N-position, and N otherwise. The original question becomes: for which n does there exist a legal first move x with (n-x,x) being P?
milestones.answer: If r \le m then N; study P/N classification for r>m \ge 1
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF normalization and P/N definitions are present
hints: Terminal win is taking all remaining

Starting from (r,1) with r>1, count the total number of moves remaining: they are exactly r, each of size 1. The player to move wins precisely when r is odd, because they take moves 1,3,...,r. Thus determine the outcome for all r.

milestones.note: ACCEPT IF parity result is correct
hints: r odd => current player takes the last match
r even => current player is forced to leave 1 match

milestones.description: For each m \ge 1 define L(m) as the smallest power of 2 strictly greater than m, i.e. L(m)=2^{\lceil \log_2(m+1)\rceil}. Claim: for every state with r>m \ge 1, the state is a P-position if and only if L(m) divides r. This fully classifies all losing positions.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF claim includes explicit L(m) and divisibility condition
decompose_advice: Prove base m=1 using the WARMUP parity result (L=2)
Induct on r: for (r,m) check all x \in [1,m]; note L(x) \le L(m) and x < L(m) | r implies r-x is never divisible by L(x)

milestones.description: Apply the classification: (r,m) is P exactly when L(m)|r. Now let n not be a power of 2 and let 2^k be the largest power of 2 with 2^k < n. Set x = n-2^k. Then 1 \le x \le n-1 and x < 2^k, so L(x) | 2^k. Taking x leaves state (2^k,x) with L(x)|2^k, hence a P-position. Thus this x is a winning first move.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF x formula correct and 1 \le x \le n-1 with x < 2^k is verified
hints: Then n-x = 2^k is divisible by L(x)

milestones.description: Now suppose n = 2^k. For any legal first move x with 1 \le x \le n-1, let L be the smallest power of 2 strictly greater than x; then L \le 2^k = n and L \nmid x. Since n-x \equiv -x \pmod L and 0<x<L, we have L \nmid (n-x). By the classification lemma (restated: (r,m) is P iff L(m)|r), the state (n-x,x) is N. Hence every move from n=2^k gives the opponent a winning position.
milestones.answer: If n=2^k then every legal move leads to an N-state; first player loses
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF modular argument L | n but L \nmid x => L \nmid n-x is used
hints: Use n \equiv 0 (mod L) and x \not\equiv 0 (mod L)

milestones.description: Assemble both directions using the classification lemma restated inside: (r,m) is P iff L(m)|r with L(m) the smallest power of 2 > m. If n is not a power of 2, write 2^k < n < 2^{k+1} and take x=n-2^k; then (2^k,x) is P, so first wins. If n=2^k, then for every legal x we have L(x) | n but L(x) \nmid n-x, so (n-x,x) is always N; thus first loses. Therefore state exactly the winning set for n>1.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF answer is exactly the set of integers n>1 that are not powers of 2

milestones.answer: Primitive prime exists for n>2 except (a,n)=(2,6)
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF exception (2,6) is included and range is n>2
hints: Define primitive divisor: does not divide earlier a^k-1

milestones.description: Assume n>2 and (a,n)≠(2,6). By Zsigmondy (restated here): there exists a prime p|a^n-1 with p∤a^k-1 for 1≤k<n; since m<n, p∤a^m-1. Thus the prime-divisor set of a^n-1 contains p while that of a^m-1 does not, contradicting equality. Hence any solution must satisfy n≤2 or (a,n)=(2,6).
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF contradiction is derived using primitive prime
decompose_advice: Separate enumeration of remaining cases n=2 and (2,6)

milestones.description: Consider n=2,m=1, the only case with n≤2 and m<n. Need the prime divisors of a-1 and (a-1)(a+1) to coincide. Note gcd(a-1,a+1)|2. If a is even, gcd=1, so any odd prime dividing a+1 is absent from a-1; since a+1>1 this is impossible. Thus a is odd and gcd=2. So every odd prime of a+1 must divide a-1, impossible unless a+1 is a power of 2. Write a=2^s-1 with s≥2. Then a-1=2(2^{s-1}-1). For its primes to be only 2, need 2^{s-1}-1=2^t. Solving 2^{s-1}-2^t=1 gives s=2,t=0, so a=3. Check: 3-1=2 and 3^2-1=8, both powers of 2.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF a=3 is derived with m=1,n=2 implied
decompose_advice: Split parity/gcd argument into its own step
Split exponential Diophantine 2^{s-1}-1=2^t into its own step

Compute: 2^1-1=1 (empty), 2^2-1=3 ({3}), 2^3-1=7 ({7}), 2^4-1=15 ({3,5}), 2^5-1=31 ({31}). None equal {3,7}, so no solution here.

milestones.note: ACCEPT IF recurrence and product P are correctly defined with cyclic index.
hints: Set x_{n+1}=x_1 and solve for x_{i+1}
Define P as the product of all x_i

milestones.description: Define f(x)=k/(C-x) = (0\cdot x+k)/((-1)x+C). Represent f by matrix M=[[0,k],[-1,C]], so f(x_i)=x_{i+1}. Then f^n(x_1)=x_1. Since the x_i are not all equal, x_1 is not a fixed point of f; for n>2 this forces f^n to be the identity transformation, hence M^n is a scalar matrix.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF matrix M and the condition M^n \propto I are stated.
hints: Use orbit size >1 to force f^n=id

milestones.description: Compute M^2 = C M - k I. Define M^m = \alpha_m M + \beta_m I with \alpha_1=1, \alpha_2=C and \alpha_{m+1}=C\alpha_m-k\alpha_{m-1}, \beta_{m+1}=-k\alpha_m. The characteristic polynomial is \lambda^2-C\lambda+k=0 with roots r,s=(C\pm\sqrt{D})/2, D=C^2-4k. If r\neq s then \alpha_m=(r^m-s^m)/(r-s). Thus M^n is scalar iff \alpha_n=0 iff (r/s)^n=1 with r\neq s.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF recurrence for \alpha_m and root condition are correct.
decompose_advice: Compute M^2 directly from matrix multiplication
Use characteristic roots r,s to solve \alpha_n=0

milestones.description: From r s=k and |r/s|=1 get |r|^2=k so |r|=\sqrt{k}. Write r=\sqrt{k}e^{i\theta}, s=\sqrt{k}e^{-i\theta}, hence C=r+s=2\sqrt{k}\cos\theta. Then (r/s)^n=e^{2in\theta}=1 gives \theta=j\pi/q with q|n, gcd(j,q)=1. So C^2/k=4\cos^2(j\pi/q). For C,k rational, k>0, need \sqrt{k}\cos(j\pi/q)\in\mathbb{Q}. If q is odd and q>3 then \cos(j\pi/q) generates a field of degree >2, impossible for rational k\neq0. Hence q=3, giving \cos^2(\pi/3)=1/4 and therefore C^2=k. Also 3|n.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF only q=3 survives and C^2=k with 3|n.
decompose_advice: Derive C^2/k = 4 cos^2(j\pi/q) from r,s form
Apply rationality conditions on cos(2\pi/q) for odd q>3

milestones.description: Write k=m^2 with m\in\mathbb{Z}^+, so C=\pm m. Then D=C^2-4k=-3m^2<0 and the roots are m\omega,m\omega^2 with \omega^3=1. Thus f^3(x)=x for all x, and f has order 3. Since n is odd and 3|n, write n=3t with t odd. Choose any rational x_1 not root of x^2-Cx+k=0 (roots are non-rational); then x_2,x_3 are rational and the sequence has exact period 3.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF normalization to square k and period 3 is correct.
hints: Check roots of x^2-Cx+k=0 are not rational

milestones.description: For C=\pm m, k=m^2, use x_{i+1}(C-x_i)=m^2. Define Q=x_1x_2x_3. From x_3=m^2/(C-x_2) and x_2=m^2/(C-x_1), substitute into Q to get Q = x_1 x_2 m^2/(C-x_2) = -C k = -C m^3 = \mp m^3. Hence Q=-Ck=\mp k^{3/2}.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF Q equals \mp k^{3/2}.
hints: Use x_3 = k/(C-x_2) and substitute x_2

milestones.description: With n=3t and t=n/3 (t is odd), the full product is P=Q^t=(\mp k^{3/2})^t=(\mp 1)^t k^{3t/2}=\mp k^{n/2}. Thus (x_1\cdots x_n)^2=k^n, and specifically x_1\cdots x_n = \pm k^{n/2}, the sign matching C=\pm\sqrt{k}.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF product formula is \pm k^{n/2} with square k^n.
hints: Use t odd to fix the sign

milestones.note: ACCEPT IF explicit example yields -8 and matches formula.

milestones.description: Need smallest integer k>1 allowing odd n>2018. From normalization k=m^2 with m\geq 2 and 3|n. The smallest square is 4 (m=2). Take n=2019=3\cdot673>2018 and the orbit (1,4,-2) repeated. Thus k=4 works, and k=2,3 fail since C^2=k is not rational. Hence the least value is 4.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF minimal k is 4 with n=2019 justification.

milestones.description: Assemble the answers. From milestones 5-7: for every valid configuration k=m^2, n=3t (t odd), and x_1\cdots x_n = \pm k^{n/2} (so the square is k^n). From milestone 9 the smallest admissible k is 4 (achieved at n=2019). Therefore part a gives the product formula and part b gives the minimal k.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF both parts are present: product \pm k^{n/2} and least k=4.

milestones.description: In parallelogram ABCD set AB = CD = a, BC = AD = b with a > b, and let h_a = AE be the height to base CD (E on CD or its extension). Define the interior angles θ and π - θ, so that sin θ = h_a / b. The parallelogram area is S = a h_a and perimeter P = 2(a+b). The disk has radius r and its center runs over all four sides; denote by F the area of the union of all such disks.
milestones.answer: S = a h_a, P = 2(a+b), sin θ = h_a/b
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF all three relations present; ALLOW equivalent forms.
hints: Perimeter is sum of all four sides

milestones.description: Without loss of generality partition the covered region U into U_out = U \ ABCD (outside within distance r) and U_in = U ∩ ABCD (inside within distance r). Then F = Area(U_out) + Area(U_in).
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF partition into outside and inside is stated.
hints: Distance to boundary ≤ r defines U

milestones.description: Consider only one side of length L. The union of disks of radius r centered on that segment is a stadium: a rectangle L × 2r plus two semicircles of radius r at the ends. Compute its area.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF formula 2rL + πr² given.
hints: Two semicircles make one full circle of area πr²

milestones.description: Apply the stadium result to each side: two sides of length a and two of length b. Summing the four capsule areas gives a preliminary total before subtracting vertex overlaps. State this sum.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF sum equals 4r(a+b)+4πr².

milestones.description: For any convex planar body with perimeter P, the area of points outside but within distance r is P·r + π·r². Apply this to the parallelogram with P = 2(a+b).
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF formula uses P=2(a+b).
hints: This is the outer parallel body minus the body itself

milestones.description: For a convex quadrilateral with interior angles θ_i and perimeter P, if r does not exceed half the smallest opposite-side distance, then Area(U_in) = P·r - r² Σ_{i=1}^{4} cot(θ_i/2). State this identity.
milestones.answer: Area(U_in) = P r - r² Σ cot(θ_i/2)
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF identity correct with sum over four angles.
hints: Derived from offsetting each side inward by r

milestones.description: For the parallelogram, θ_1 = θ_3 = θ and θ_2 = θ_4 = π - θ with sin θ = h_a/b. Compute C = cot(θ/2) + cot((π-θ)/2) + cot(θ/2) + cot((π-θ)/2). Use cot((π-θ)/2) = tan(θ/2) and 1/(sin(θ/2)cos(θ/2)) = 2/sin θ.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF C = 4b/h_a.

milestones.description: Using P = 2(a+b) and C = 4b/h_a, compute Area(U_in) valid for r ≤ h_a/2.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF expression matches.
hints: Substitute P and C into the lemma

milestones.description: Check consistency at r = h_a/2: Area(U_in) should equal the full parallelogram area a h_a. Verify using the formula from the previous step.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF equality simplifies to a h_a.

milestones.description: For r ≤ h_a/2 combine Area(U_out) = 2(a+b)r + π r² and Area(U_in) = 2(a+b)r - (4b/h_a)r² to obtain F.
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF formula correct for this case.

milestones.description: Restate both cases: if r ≤ h_a/2 then F = 4(a+b)r + (π - 4b/h_a)r²; if r ≥ h_a/2 then U_in fills the parallelogram so Area(U_in) = a h_a while Area(U_out) remains 2(a+b)r + π r². Assemble the final piecewise result.
milestones.answer: F = \begin{cases} 4(a+b)r + (\pi - 4b/h_a)r² & r \leq h_a/2 \\ a h_a + 4(a+b)r + \pi r² & r \geq h_a/2 \end{cases}
milestones.note: ACCEPT IF piecewise matches both branches exactly.
hints: Inside is fully covered when r reaches half the height h_a/2
